messages:
maya: Customer on enterprise plan reporting intermittent 401s from web app only when it's embedded in a third-party iframe on Vercel preview deploys. If they open the app directly, auth works.

sam: Did they say which SDK/version? Browser console shows 401 or 'No Authorization header'?

maya: They sent logs from support portal – browser shows 401 on POST /v1/generate, server logs indicate missing Authorization header. Using our edge TS SDK in the frontend bundle (redwood-edge-sdk@0.7.0). Repro steps included.

eli: interesting. Vercel previews insert an intermediate redirect+proxy sometimes. redirects can drop credentials depending on fetch settings. Can you paste the fetch/SDK init they're using?

maya: Here's the snippet they shared:

```ts
import { Redwood } from 'redwood-edge-sdk'
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_RW_KEY })

// client used directly in browser bundle
await client.generate({ model: 'gpt-4o-mini', input: 'hi' })
```

The app is embedded in an iframe on a partner site. Their dev said cookies were set with SameSite=None and Secure.

juno: @eli could this be SameSite or credential-mode related? If the request goes through a redirect, some runtimes re-create the request without credentials.

eli: Yep. Two separate failure modes here:
1) If the browser is doing a redirect (307) from a preview proxy, fetch can drop Authorization unless credentials are included and not on cross-origin simple requests.
2) Our edge SDK's internal fetch wrapper (pre-0.7.2) intentionally normalized headers for edge bundles and would remove Authorization on a redirect path to avoid leaking tokens to upstream in some host configs. That behavior is unsafe for iframe-hosted single-page apps.

sam: That's likely it — they are on 0.7.0. We patched this in 0.8.2 to preserve Authorization on same-origin rewrites and to allow an opt-in credentials include.

maya: Customer tried adding credentials: 'include' to fetch but since SDK abstracts fetch they couldn't. Quick repro they provided (vanilla fetch) shows it works when credentials included.

eli: Workarounds:
- Short term: have them upgrade to redwood-edge-sdk@0.8.2 (we shipped a fix to preserve auth and expose fetchOptions.credentials for edge bundles).
- If upgrade isn't possible, use a tiny proxy route in Next.js API route (server-side) to forward requests — keeps token server-side and avoids browser token leaks in iframe.

juno: Also note: Vercel preview proxies sometimes change the request URL (internal path) which triggers a preflight OPTIONS that our CDN cached with 204 and no Authorization. Ask them to disable Options caching for the route in their preview settings or set Access-Control-Max-Age to 0 while debugging.

maya: Sharing repro steps we asked the customer to run:
1) Create a minimal Next.js preview deploy with the same SDK bundle (0.7.0).
2) Embed the preview URL in an external iframe on a different origin.
3) Open DevTools -> Network -> Preserve logs and trigger a generate call.
4) Check if the request goes 307 -> POST and whether Authorization is in the final request headers.

sam: If anyone needs a quick trace helper, here's a fetch wrapper they can drop into the page for debugging:

```js
window.__rw_traceFetch = async (url, opts={}) => {
  const res = await fetch(url, opts)
  console.log('trace', { url, opts, status: res.status, headers: [...res.headers] })
  return res
}
```

deploy-bot: Deployed preview patch branch "fix/edge-credentials-0.8.2" to staging (pv-1234) :rocket:

eli: I'll follow up with a tiny SDK patch note and example on the support ticket. Also add an entry in the edge runtime docs about redirects and credentials.

maya: Customer is trying the upgrade now — will update when they confirm. TY :thumbsup:

sam: If they still see 401 after upgrade, ask for HAR file and the server-side logs showing the exact request we received (headers). That will let us tell whether the header was stripped client-side or at the proxy.

maya: ack, thanks all :eyes:
